_note: Committed, dated reference gazetteer of PORTS for the maritime collector bbox. Loaded ONCE in-process and NEVER fetched at runtime (mirrors backend/data/airports_aoi.json, zones_aoi.json, mmsi_mid.json). PORT-1: ASSET + LOADER ONLY -- no sessionization, no port_visit events, no composite wiring (that is PORT-2, annotation-only, and the composite is deliberately never wired: PORT-pre measured that admitting port visits would grow the composite 9-68% with routine commerce).

manifest.scope: The maritime collector bbox: 12-42N, 24-63.5E. The WPI spine covers the whole bbox (180 features). The OSM supplement is deliberately TARGETED, not a sweep -- see sources.OSM.selection and deferred.gulf_theater_osm_supplement.

syria_lebanon_coverage.why_it_matters: The AOI centres on Syria. WPI -- the public-domain spine -- carries ZERO Syrian ports (no Latakia, no Tartus, no Baniyas), ONE Lebanese entry (Sayda/Sidon, harborSize 'V' = very small, harborType 'OR' = open roadstead), and NO Beirut. A gazetteer blind to the AOI's home ports would be close to useless there, so the OSM supplement targets exactly this hole.

syrian_ports_named_in_the_requirement.Baniyas: present WITH A CAVEAT (OSM node/1001586641) -- tagged amenity=ferry_terminal, not a harbour/port polygon, and the OFFSHORE OIL TERMINAL is absent from OSM entirely. Recorded as a documented limitation on the feature (source_note); a coordinate was NOT invented for the SPM moorings.

lebanese_ports_named_in_the_requirement.Tripoli: present (OSM way/777711541, industrial=port, Tripoli Port Authority)

WPI.coordinate_precision: Pub 150 s3, verbatim: "The position of each port, expressed in degrees and minutes, is generally obtained from the best-scale chart available." MEASURED against that claim: 356 of 360 AOI coordinate components carry seconds = 00; the 4 exceptions are whole seconds; NO AOI record carries sub-minute precision. (55 of 2,951 global records have been re-surveyed to fractional-second precision -- 46 of them Italian -- and NONE is in the AOI.) So +/- ~0.93 km lat / ~0.78 km lon at 33N. No datum is stated in the publication.
WPI.vintage: NOT AVAILABLE from the source. The API payload is a bare {"ports":[...]} with no manifest and no Last-Modified header, so this asset stamps its own captured_at and cites NO edition. The printed publication is the 24th Edition, 2015 (current to 13 Dec 2014); the live API is plainly newer but undated.
WPI.per_feature_provenance: source_ref carries the WPI globalId GUID; the stable portNumber is embedded in port_id.

OSM.name: OpenStreetMap
OSM.geometry: polygon centroid (way/relation) or point placement (node); metre-level placement, so unlike WPI the radius carries no positional-error budget
OSM.odbl_obligation: ODbL requires attribution AND share-alike. This committed extract is a Produced Work derived from OSM: the attribution above is carried in this manifest AND every OSM-derived feature is individually tagged source='OSM' with its openstreetmap.org element URL in source_ref and its originating tags in osm_tags, so the obligation is traceable PER FEATURE. Any redistribution of this asset or a database derived from it must preserve the attribution and, for the OSM-derived subset, the ODbL share-alike terms. The WPI-derived subset carries no such obligation.
OSM.selection: TARGETED, not opportunistic. (1) The Syria/Lebanon commercial harbours WPI omits entirely -- queried by name (Latakia/اللاذقية, Tartus/طرطوس, Baniyas/بانياس, Beirut/بيروت, Tripoli/طرابلس) and by tag over the Levant coast. (2) Two East-Med harbours WPI lacks that are >10 km from any WPI AOI port (Vasilikos, Moni -- Cyprus). Every one of the 10 was individually tag-inspected before inclusion.

exclusions_applied.pure_marinas_and_small_craft: Excluded per PORT-pre, which found the OSM named harbour set is dominated by them. This rejected two features whose ARABIC names read as ports but whose OSM tags are leisure=marina + seamark:harbour:category=marina: Arwad (way/1126981953, مرفأ أرواد) and Ras al-Basit fishing port (way/166349018). Excluded on the tag, not on the name.
exclusions_applied.inland_dry_ports: An AOI-wide industrial=port / man_made=port / seamark:harbour:category query returned 180 unique elements, 134 named and non-marina. Several are INLAND logistics facilities tagged industrial=port -- Riyadh Dry Port, SAUDIA CARGO, Khazaen Dry Port (455-1158 km from the nearest AOI coast) and Gunaydin Group Lojistik Merkezi (measured inland_depth_km = 56.4 via backend.geo_area). A maritime port gazetteer must not carry them.
exclusions_applied.terminal_level_fragments: The same query returns individual berths/terminals inside ports the WPI spine already carries -- 7 Khalifa Port features, 4 Jebel Ali container terminals, 2 AHMED BIN RASHID PORT nodes, 3 duplicate Ras Tanura nodes. Admitting them would fragment one port into many overlapping circles and flood merges_with. Excluded; 75 of the 134 named candidates sat within 10 km of an existing WPI port.

OSM.query: Overpass: (a) Levant box 33.0-36.2N, 35.0-36.4E for seamark:type=harbour / landuse=harbour / harbour=yes / industrial=port / man_made=port / named landuse=industrial; (b) a Baniyas-specific name+tag query; (c) an AOI-wide seamark:harbour:category ~ commercial|fishing|cargo|tanker + industrial=port + man_made=port sweep in five sub-boxes, used to CHECK for omissions rather than to bulk-import (see exclusions_applied).
OSM.alternate_name_policy: Drawn from each element's OSM name:ar / name:en / name:fr / alt_name tags, PLUS standard English transliterations (Baniyas/Banias for OSM's 'Banyas', Lattakia, Tartous, Beyrouth, Tyre/Sour) so the search field is reachable by the spelling a user actually types. alternate_name is a SEARCH AID, not a claim about the port; the authoritative name is port_name.

considered_and_rejected.UN/LOCODE: ODC-PDDL (public domain), 103,034 locations. REJECTED AS GEOMETRY: coordinates are DDMM[N/S] DDDMM[W/E] -- degree-and-minute, the same or worse than WPI -- and frequently empty. Retained only as a JOIN KEY: the unlocode field, which WPI already supplies for 89% of the AOI set.
considered_and_rejected.EMODnet Human Activities Main Ports: Eurostat-derived, POINTS not polygons, and EU + Norway/Turkey/UK/Montenegro scope only -- no Israel, Lebanon, Syria or Egypt, i.e. blind to exactly the hole this asset had to fill. Licence not verified. Rejected as a source; usable later as an EU/Turkey coordinate cross-check.

geometry_policy.form: POINT + radius_m. NO polygons. PORT-pre measured OSM harbour-polygon coverage across the AOI at only ~18% of harbour features and inconsistent; WPI has no extent field at all. A polygon-first design is not supportable on open sources.
geometry_policy.radius_basis: 'assumed' on EVERY feature -- no source in this asset publishes a measured harbour extent. This is WEAKER than zones_aoi.json, where 29 of 36 features were 'sourced' (the UNCLOS Art. 60(5) 500 m safety zone on surveyed platform points). Stated here rather than buried: no port radius in this asset is evidence of anything, it is a search aperture.
geometry_policy.radius_scale_wpi_basis: ASSUMED: scaled by WPI harborSize (V 1.5 / S 2.5 / M 3.5 / L 5.0 km). WPI carries no extent field, so no radius here is measured. The 1.5 km floor is set by WPI's own coordinate precision -- Pub 150 gives positions in degrees and MINUTES (+/- ~0.93 km lat, ~0.78 km lon at 33N, ~1.2 km diagonal) -- so a smaller circle could miss the real harbour entirely. For a 'V' harbour the positional error EXCEEDS the harbour, so the radius is an uncertainty budget, not an extent.

coord_precision_values.arcminute: WPI -- degrees and minutes (Pub 150 s3); +/- ~1 km. 178 of 180.
coord_precision_values.arcsecond: WPI -- whole non-zero seconds present (Al Fujayrah, Khawr Fakkan). 2 of 180; labelled honestly rather than blanket-tagged arcminute.
coord_precision_values.polygon_centroid: OSM way/relation reduced to its centroid.

geometry_policy.merges_with: Symmetric per-feature list of the OTHER port_ids this feature cannot be cleanly distinguished from: centres within 6.0 km, OR the two assumed circles overlap. PORT-pre measured 15 WPI AOI pairs within 6 km (tightest Gebze <-> Kaba Burnu at 1.4 km, Borusan Fertilizer Jetty <-> Gemlik 1.41, Antalya <-> Antalya Offshore Terminal 2.37, Haydarpasa <-> Istanbul 4.59). Any usable radius merges distinct terminals, so attribution ambiguity is DATA: PORT-2 must be able to say 'this session is attributable to either X or Y', never silently pick the first match.

known_limits: radius_basis is 'assumed' on every feature; no measured extent exists.

WPI coordinates are degrees-and-minutes BY PUBLICATION DESIGN (+/- ~1 km), with no datum stated -- comparable to the radius itself for the 107 'V' harbours, where the positional error exceeds the harbour.

A cross-check against OSM found WPI's Sayda (Sidon, Lebanon) point sits ~7.3 km from the OSM Port of Sidon polygon centroid -- 7x WPI's own stated precision, so that entry looks misplaced, not merely rounded. Recorded on the feature as coord_crosscheck; the WPI point was NOT silently overwritten.
PORT-pre measured only 43 of 180 WPI AOI ports producing any vessel session over 16 days. A silent port is a COVERAGE fact, not a mis-sited feature.

WPI harborSize can be STALE, and the radius is scaled from it, so the radius inherits the staleness. Measured at PORT-1: WPI classifies Ambarli (Istanbul) as 'V' = very small, giving it the 1.5 km floor -- but PORT-pre found Ambarli in the collector's densest 1-degree cell with 1,046 vessels in a 0.25deg vicinity, and the 1.5 km circle captures only 26. A size-derived radius UNDER-COVERS any port whose WPI size class is out of date. PORT-2 must treat a low in-radius vessel count at a known-major port as a GEOMETRY signal, not a traffic one.
Baniyas is carried as an amenity=ferry_terminal node; its offshore oil terminal is absent from OSM and is NOT represented.
This asset is reference geometry only. It emits no fact about any vessel. Sessionization is PORT-2 and is annotation-only.

listed_ports.reason: NO PORT-KEYED SOURCE EXISTS TO FREEZE. Re-confirmed at PORT-pre from the primary documents: OFAC's Syria shipping advisories (e.g. 2024-09-11) designate VESSELS -- an annex of hulls blocked on the SDN List -- not ports as places; no open sanctions list (OFAC/EU/UN/UK) enumerates ports as geography. And designation is a DATED LEGAL STATE that has since moved decisively: Syria's core sanctions EO was revoked 2025-06-30 and the Caesar Act was REPEALED 2025-12-18 by the FY2026 NDAA. So a citations-only snapshot would be a snapshot of prose that names hulls -- it would yield no port features at all. Reversible only if a port-keyed designation source appears, and then only in the UCS-2023 badge form: a frozen dated snapshot, each entry citing issuing body and document date, rendering 'named in [document], [date]' and NEVER 'sanctioned port' as standing fact.

gap_toward_a_port_signal.reason: MEASURED ANTI-CORRELATED at PORT-pre, so there is nothing to revisit. Against a null baseline of 19.19% of all plausible fixes lying within 15 km of a test port, only 8.2% of A1 candidate gaps START there and 7.6% END there -- depleted ~2.3x, because A1's waterfall already bins near-port gaps as 'stationary' (59.7% of gaps starting within 15 km of a port). Course consistency toward the port was 26.0% against a 25.0% uniform-course expectation: chance. Both halves null simultaneously.

gulf_theater_osm_supplement.reason: SCOPE, not a data gap -- and narrower than it sounds: the WPI spine DOES cover the Gulf (Iran 12, Saudi Arabia 10, UAE 9, Iraq 6, Kuwait 6, Qatar 6, Bahrain 4, Oman 4 ports are all present). What is deferred is only the OSM SUPPLEMENT there, where the AOI-wide query returned mostly terminal-level fragments of ports WPI already carries (7 Khalifa Port, 4 Jebel Ali terminals) and inland dry ports. Consistent with zones_aoi.json's Gulf/Iran theater deferral. Reversible.

port_visit_composite_admission.reason: Not a phase gate -- a measured decision. PORT-pre: admitting port visits would touch 641 of 1,727 composite hulls, flip 604 from 1 to 2 pattern_types and add 538 new hulls (68% growth); even the tightest bar (complete, fully-bracketed visits) flips 96 hulls and grows it 9%. Because composite_rank promotes n_pattern_types == 2 to HIGH on a grey flag or a high underlying event, that would manufacture high-rank hulls out of a cargo ship calling at Haifa. Port visits are routine commerce (~45% of measured visits are ferry/leisure/tug). No migration, no n_port_visit column, no sig-CTE disjunct.
